pull.title: KAFKA-20579: Implement compression support for KIP-1332
pull.body:
This PR implements support for compression with the incremental producer
allocation strategy, which requires handling of edge cases where more
chunks are needed mid write.

Reviewers: Nikita Shupletsov <nikita@shupletsov.ca>, Lianet Magrans <lmagrans@confluent.io>, Jun Rao <junrao@gmail.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
thank you. LGTM.
@lianetm could you please take a look?

Thanks @ezhou413! Took a first high level look. 

Could you also please look at REcordAccumulatorTest, and enable compression-related tests for "incremental" ? (see my comment here https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23135#discussion_r3769371194 )
@ezhou413 : Thanks for the PR. Left a few comments.

review_comments.body: I don't think we fall through here

shouldn't we do this check before we actually call pool.deallocate? this this order we can deallocate something that doesn't belong to the pool. I think that's the point of having poolAllocatedChunks? please correct me if I am wrong

I assume the logic was taken from MemoryRecordsBuilder.estimatedBytesWritten. but there we also use CompressionRatioEstimator.estimation, which tracks previous compression rates for the topic.
I don't necessarily think we need to do it here, but I am also not sure if adding these 5% on top will do much for us here
Yep you're right, updated this section
As I understand it, `interrupt()` doesn't immediately stop the thread, so we still are able to get to the else section below (since `next = null`)
Reverted this change

an alternative could be using Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>()); for poolAllocatedChunks. then we would not need this method.
but completely up to you
is there a situation when the pool is null?

I took a deeper look into allocateChunks.
It creates conditions, updates the waiters list, waits for exactly 0ms, and so on. so there is quite a bit of unnecessary work when we pass 0 here. so, basically, the whole else block is unnecessary: https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/trunk/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/internals/BufferPool.java#L310-L365

we could simplify the path there if 0 is passed. or, as claude suggested, we could create a separate method: tryAllocateChunks, which would return null instead of throwing BufferExhaustedException. it may be a cleaner way, but needs a deeper look into it

if would be also good to test the same situation(high entropy messages with compression rate above 1), but with the initial estimation significantly lower than 1. so we can verify that we correctly handle the situation when we allowed way more data into one batch than its size
Good call, didn't know about this. thanks!
Not right now. But since this class is public it's possible if it's used elsewhere in the future
I added a case in BufferPool to fail fast if we pass 0
added a test
I think we don't need this branch, because we added tryAllocateChunks
I think it would be cleaner if we returned pooled instead of passing it in as a parameter and expecting side effects
because we are deplicating the logic from the CompressionRatioEstimator, it will always be correct. maybe it makes sense to use the exact numbers here, as we know exactly what data we send
Removed

we want to use the compressed estimation based on the ratio (not the uncompressed one).

We did consider using uncompressed estimation here but ended up rejecting it (https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/KAFKA/pages/421957499/KIP-1332+Dynamic+memory+allocation+for+the+Kafka+producer#KIP1332%3ADynamicmemoryallocationfortheKafkaproducer-RejectedAlternatives)

passing `chunkSize` here means we'll allocate 1 chunk at a time, right? is that the intention?

This case I expect it's to cover the compressor flushing more than what we have reserved. That may not be rare depending on the estimations I expect, and one a time means acquiring lock, trying the pool etc.  

So should we consider trying to allocate all the chunks we need (try to get as much as we can from the poll first, then fall back to the heap for whatever is left).  We still need this `tryAllocateChunks` that does all or nothing when allocating from the extension path (allocateExtensionChunks), but when called from the write path (this), what about having an approach of "tryAppendChunksUpTo"...the needs are different imo

> without reserving anything

this related to the above comment, when the extra chunks are needing when writing, what about trying to allocate as much as we can from the pool? If we do all-or-nothing we could end up falling back to heap allocation from more than what's really needed.

Is this necessary? This call never increases memory and is never called from a waiter.
Should we verify that the compressor actually overshoots?

Claude found the following issue.

`tryAllocateChunks() can starve threads blocked waiting for memory (BufferPool.java:383). reserveChunksIfAvailable only checks free memory and ignores the waiters queue. Mid-write growth by appenders, and by the sender when it closes compressed batches during drain, can take freed chunks ahead of a thread blocked in allocateChunks. Under steady pressure that thread can hit BufferExhaustedException at max.block.ms even though memory keeps being freed. The full strategy doesn't have this problem because it grows on the heap. One option: refuse when !waiters.isEmpty() and use the heap instead.`
What's the convention of calling resetEstimation at the end of the test? Should it be reset if the test changes the estimator? If so, this test changes that.

review_comments.body:
Claude found the following.

`A closed pool is reported as memory exhaustion (ChunkedRecordAccumulator.java:178). When the pool is closed, the extension path sets nonBlockingMemoryAllocationDenied = true and loops. throwIfNoMoreRetriesAllowed runs before tryAppend's closed check. So if the deadline has already passed, the send fails with BufferExhaustedException and increments the buffer-exhausted metric, instead of KafkaException("Producer closed …"). This also changes what the caller sees: BufferExhaustedException is an ApiException, so the callback fires and a failed future is returned instead of send() throwing. The window is narrow, but the javadoc at :286-287 describes a different order than the code.`

In the uncompressed case, we should never hit this path. So, keeping the IllegalStateException in the uncompressed case is potentially useful. SingleByteBufferOutputStream has the same issue. So, this is an existing issue and could be addressed in the future.
The comment is inaccurate. The accumulator never calls throwIfInsufficientRemaining(). This method is test only. It would be useful document that in the javadoc.
In RecordAccumulatorTest, the large-append, split and ratio tests still run only with the FULL strategy. Should we extend that to INCREMENTAL too?
